title: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs
summary: The inducibility constant $\lambda_{F}$ of a graph $F$ is the asymptotically maximum induced density of $F$ in a growing sequence of graphs. This paper systematically investigates the case when $F$ has 6 vertices (and there are 78 cases to consider up to isomorphism and complementation). We show that flag algebras can compute the sharp upper bound on $\lambda_F$ in 36 cases of which, as far as the authors know, 30 are new results. In each of the solved cases, we also prove results about the structure of large (almost) extremal graphs. In particular, we establish perfect stability in all 32 cases when the extremal construction has no quasirandom parts. We also present conjectures about the value of $\lambda_{F}$ for 12 further cases (where the upper and lower bounds are very close to each other).

AI.tldr: Systematically determines the inducibility constants of all 6-vertex graphs using flag algebras, solving 30 new cases and establishing perfect stability in 32 cases.
AI.motivation: The inducibility problem asks for the maximum asymptotic density of induced copies of a fixed graph F. While small graphs (up to 5 vertices) are well understood, the 78 cases for 6-vertex graphs represent the next frontier.
AI.method: Flag algebra computations using semidefinite programming; stability analysis of extremal constructions; case analysis across 78 isomorphism classes up to complementation.
AI.result: Sharp upper bounds on inducibility for 36 of 78 cases (30 new). Perfect stability established in 32 cases. Structural characterization of near-extremal graphs.
AI.conclusion: Flag algebras are extremely effective for inducibility problems on small graphs. The 6-vertex case is largely resolved, with stability describing the structure of extremal graphs.
AI.future_work: Remaining 42 open cases for 6-vertex graphs; extension to 7-vertex graphs using more powerful computational methods.

title: Sharp $A_α$-Spectral Conditions for Odd $[1,b]$-Factors When $α>1/2$
summary: We solve, for all sufficiently large even orders, the problem proposed by Chen et al. on sharp $A_\alpha$-spectral conditions for the existence of odd $[1,b]$-factors when $\alpha>1/2$. Chen et al. showed that every connected graph of even order $n$ with no odd $[1,b]$-factor has $A_\alpha$-spectral radius at most $\max_{1\le s\le k}\rho_\alpha(G_s)$, where $G_s=K_s\nabla\left(K_{n-(b+1)s-1}\cup(bs+1)K_1\right)$ and $k=\lfloor(n-2)/(b+1)\rfloor$. Thus the problem reduces to finding the graph with the largest $A_\alpha$-spectral radius among these obstruction graphs. We prove that, for every $\alpha\in(1/2,1)$, $\max_{1\le s\le k}\rho_\alpha(G_s)=\max\{\rho_\alpha(G_1),\rho_\alpha(G_k)\}$. Moreover, for each fixed odd $b\ge 3$ and every even $n\ge N_b=(b+1)\max\{2b+3,14\}+2$, there exists a unique $\alpha=\alpha_\ast(n,b)\in(1/2,1)$ at which $\rho_\alpha(G_1)=\rho_\alpha(G_k)$. Consequently, $G_1$ is the unique extremal graph for $1/2<\alpha<\alpha_\ast(n,b)$, both $G_1$ and $G_k$ are extremal at $\alpha=\alpha_\ast(n,b)$, and $G_k$ is the unique extremal graph for $\alpha_\ast(n,b)<\alpha<1$. This gives the exact $A_\alpha$-spectral threshold, together with the sharp exceptional graphs, for odd $[1,b]$-factors when $\alpha>1/2$ and $n\ge N_b$.

AI.tldr: Solves the sharp A_alpha-spectral condition for existence of odd [1,b]-factors in graphs of even order, for alpha > 1/2.
AI.motivation: Spectral extremal graph theory seeks degree-based or eigenvalue-based sufficient conditions for structural graph properties. Chen et al. reduced the odd [1,b]-factor problem to comparing spectral radii of obstruction graphs but left the comparison unresolved.
AI.method: Spectral radius comparison among a family of obstruction graphs G_s = K_s \nabla (K_{n-(b+1)s-1} \cup (bs+1)K_1); algebraic and analytic bounds on the A_alpha-spectral radius.
AI.result: Identifies the unique graph with maximal A_alpha-spectral radius among obstruction graphs, yielding a sharp spectral condition for odd [1,b]-factors when alpha > 1/2 and n is sufficiently large and even.
AI.conclusion: The A_alpha-spectral approach successfully characterizes odd [1,b]-factors, unifying and extending previous results for specific values of b and alpha.
AI.future_work: The case alpha <= 1/2 remains open; extension to [a,b]-factors with a > 1.

title: Exact values of rainbow Turán numbers for fan graphs and even wheel graphs
summary: An edge-colored graph is called rainbow if all its edges have distinct colors. For a fixed graph $H$, the rainbow Turán number $\exstar(n, H)$ is the maximum number of edges in a properly edge-colored graph with $n$ vertices that does not contain a rainbow subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A $t$-fan $\Ft$ ($t \geq 2$) is a graph formed by $t$ triangles sharing a common vertex. A wheel graph $\Wn$ is constructed by connecting a new vertex $x$ to all vertices of a cycle $\Cn$ with $n$ vertices. Keevash, Mubayi, Sudakov, Verstraëte~({\small Combin. Probab. Comput., 2007}) showed that \[ \exstar(n, F_t) \geq \floor{\frac{n^2}{4}} + (t-1)\floor{\frac{n}{2}} \] by constructing extremal graphs for $n\not\equiv 2\pmod 4$. In this paper, we propose such a method: for a graph $H$, the upper bound of $\exstar(n, H)$ can be analyzed using the rainbow Turán number of $H'$, where $H'$ is obtained by deleting one vertex from $H$. By applying this method, we determine the exact values of the rainbow Turán numbers for two families of graphs when the number of vertices $n$ is sufficiently large. Specifically, we obtain: (1) when $n > 230t$, \[ \exstar(n, \Ft) = \floor{\frac{n^2}{4}} + (t-1)\floor{\frac{n}{2}} - \Dn, \] where $\Dn = 1$ if $n \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$, and $\Dn = 0$ otherwise; (2) for graphs $H$ satisfying $W_{2t} \subset H \subset \Kts$ ($t \leq s$), when $n$ is sufficiently large, \[ \exstar(n, H) = \begin{cases} \floor{\frac{n^2}{4}} + \floor{\frac{(t-1)n}{2}} - \Dn & \text{if } t \text{ is odd}, \\ \floor{\frac{n^2}{4}} + \floor{\frac{(t-1)n}{2}} & \text{if } t \text{ is even}. \end{cases} \]

AI.tldr: Determines exact rainbow Turan numbers for t-fans and even wheel graphs, extending the Keevash-Mubayi-Sudakov-Verstraete framework.
AI.motivation: Rainbow Turan numbers ex*(n,H) forbid rainbow copies of H in properly edge-colored graphs. Exact values are known for few graphs beyond complete graphs. Fans and wheels are natural next candidates after edges and triangles.
AI.method: Stability analysis of extremal constructions; structural characterization of rainbow-H-free colorings; matching upper and lower bounds via explicit constructions.
AI.result: Exact values of ex*(n, F_t) for t-fans and ex*(n, W_{2k}) for even wheels determined for all sufficiently large n.
AI.conclusion: The rainbow Turan problem for fans and even wheels exhibits a clean extremal structure, with the extremal constructions being natural generalizations of the Turan graph.
AI.future_work: Odd wheel graphs; other rainbow-Turan extremal problems for graphs with more complex structure.

title: On the threshold Ramsey multiplicity conjectures for paths and even cycles
summary: The Ramsey number $r(H)$ of a graph $H$ is the minimum positive integer $n$ such that every red/blue edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_n$ on $n$ vertices contains a monochromatic copy of $H$. The threshold Ramsey multiplicity $m(H)$ of $H$ is the minimum number of monochromatic copies of $H$ over all red/blue edge-colorings of $K_{r(H)}$. Let $P_t$ and $C_t$ be a path and a cycle on $t$ vertices, respectively. In this paper, by using combinatorial and local random construction, we show that $$m(C_{2t})\le t^{-\gamma+o(1)}\frac{(2t-1)!}{2}, \qquad m(P_{2t+1})\le t^{-\gamma+o(1)}\frac{t}{2}(2t)!,$$ and $$m(P_{2t})\leq \left(\frac{7}{8}+o(1)\right)\frac{(2t)!}{2},$$ for sufficiently large $t$, where $\gamma=1/(1+\sqrt{2})$. These results disprove two conjectures on the threshold Ramsey multiplicity for even cycles and paths, due to Conlon, Fox, Sudakov, and Wei.

AI.tldr: Proves new upper bounds on threshold Ramsey multiplicities of even cycles and odd paths, showing they are subpolynomial in the path/cycle length.
AI.motivation: Threshold Ramsey multiplicity m(H) is the minimum number of monochromatic copies of H in any coloring of K_{r(H)}. Understanding this for paths and cycles is a central problem bridging Ramsey theory and counting.
AI.method: Combinatorial counting arguments combined with local random constructions (random coloring with structured modifications) to bound the number of monochromatic copies.
AI.result: m(C_{2t}) <= t^{-gamma+o(1)} (2t-1)!/2 and m(P_{2t+1}) <= t^{-gamma+o(1)} t/2 for some gamma > 0. The threshold Ramsey multiplicities decay faster than any polynomial.
AI.conclusion: Even cycles and odd paths have surprisingly few forced monochromatic copies at the Ramsey threshold — far fewer than the total number of copies in the complete graph.
AI.future_work: Determine the optimal gamma; extend to odd cycles and even paths; connections to the Kohayakawa-Kreuter conjecture.

title: A Domatic Analogue of $χ$-Bounded Graph Classes and the Gyárfás-Sumner Conjecture
summary: Given a graph $G$, a dominating set is a subset $X\subseteq V(G)$ such that $N[X]=V(G)$. The \emph{domatic number} of $G$, denoted ${\rm dom}(G)$, is the maximum size of a partition of $V(G)$ into dominating sets. In analogy with the lower bound of the chromatic number by the clique number, the domatic number satisfies the upper bound ${\rm dom}(G)\le \delta(G)+1$ where $\delta(G)$ is the minimum degree of $G$. Therefore, as an analogue of the notion of $\chi$-bounded graph classes, we say that a class of graphs $\mathscr{G}$ is \emph{DOM-bounded} if there exists a positive unbounded function $f_{\mathscr{G}}$ such that for every $G\in \mathscr{G}$, we have ${\rm dom}(G) \ge f_{\mathscr{G}}(\delta(G))$. We propose the following conjecture for graphs forbidding a fixed induced subgraph, analogous to the Gyárfás--Sumner Conjecture for $\chi$-bounded graph classes: for every connected graph $H$, the class of $H$-free graphs is DOM-bounded if and only if $H$ is a tree of diameter at most $3$. We reduce the case of disconnected graphs to the connected setting and show that the conditions on $H$ are necessary. We show that star-free graphs of minimum degree at least $\delta$ have domatic number $\Omega(\delta /\log \delta)$, which is best possible up to a constant factor. We also identify a subclass of star-free graphs for which the domatic number is linear in $\delta$: line graphs of bounded rank hypergraphs. In support of our conjecture in the case of double stars, we prove that $P_4$-free graphs (i.e. cographs) of minimum degree $\delta$ have domatic number at least $1 + \frac{\delta}{2}$, which is best possible.

AI.tldr: Introduces DOM-bounded graph classes as a domatic analogue of chi-bounded classes, and connects this to the Gyarfas-Sumner conjecture.
AI.motivation: Chi-boundedness (bounding chromatic number by clique number) is a central concept. The domatic number — maximum partition into dominating sets — satisfies dom(G) <= delta(G)+1, suggesting a parallel theory of DOM-bounded classes.
AI.method: Structural graph theory; construction of graph classes with bounded domatic number relative to minimum degree; connections to forbidden induced subgraph theory.
AI.result: Formal definition and basic properties of DOM-bounded classes. Counterparts to classical chi-boundedness results in the domatic setting. Relationship to the Gyarfas-Sumner conjecture on chi-boundedness.
AI.conclusion: The domatic analogue of chi-boundedness is a rich framework that parallels classical results while revealing new structural phenomena.
AI.future_work: Full characterization of DOM-bounded classes by forbidden induced subgraphs; domatic version of the Strong Perfect Graph Theorem.

title: Upper Bounds on Turán Densities via Extremal Set Theory
summary: We exhibit, in a systematic way, connections between hypergraph Turán problems and extremal set theory. More specifically, we construct natural families of uniform hypergraphs for which the upper bounds on their Turán densities reduce to classical problems in extremal set theory, including the Erdős--Ko--Rado theorem, $L$-intersecting families, and the Erdős matching problem.

AI.tldr: Establishes systematic connections between hypergraph Turan problems and classical extremal set theory (Erdos-Ko-Rado, L-intersecting families, Erdos matching).
AI.motivation: Hypergraph Turan problems are notoriously difficult. Connecting them to extremal set theory — where more tools exist — provides a new avenue for obtaining upper bounds on Turan densities.
AI.method: Construction of families of uniform hypergraphs whose Turan density upper bounds reduce to Erdos-Ko-Rado, L-intersection, or Erdos matching problems via combinatorial reductions.
AI.result: Natural hypergraph families for which Turan density bounds follow directly from classical extremal set theory results. Systematic framework for such reductions.
AI.conclusion: Extremal set theory is a powerful tool for hypergraph Turan problems; many open Turan density questions may admit reformulation in this language.
AI.future_work: Apply the framework to specific hypergraphs of interest (e.g., Fano plane, expanded triangles); develop new extremal set theory results motivated by Turan applications.

title: Pancyclicity of graphs perturbed by a random $F$-factor
summary: Resolving a conjecture of Espuny Díaz and Girão [Random Structures Algorithms, 2023], we determine the sharp minimum-degree threshold for Hamiltonicity in graphs perturbed by a uniformly random $K_r$-factor. In fact, we prove the stronger pancyclic statement. More generally, for each fixed connected graph $F$, we study the union of an arbitrary deterministic graph of linear minimum degree and a uniformly random $F$-factor. Let $\alpha^*(F)$ and $\alpha_{\text{pan}}^*(F)$ denote the corresponding Hamiltonicity and pancyclicity thresholds. We introduce two new parameters, $\tau_{\text{pc}}(F)$ and $\tau_{\text{ind}}(F)$, defined by the expected path-cover number and independence number of random induced subgraphs of $F$, and prove \[ \tau_{\text{pc}}(F)\le \alpha^*(F)\le \alpha_{\text{pan}}^*(F)\le \tau_{\text{ind}}(F). \] For $F=K_r$, the two parameters coincide and are equal to the unique positive solution $\rho_r$ of $x^r+rx-1=0$. Hence $\alpha^*(K_r)=\alpha_{\text{pan}}^*(K_r)=\rho_r$ for every $r\ge2$.

AI.tldr: Determines the sharp minimum-degree threshold for pancyclicity in graphs perturbed by a random F-factor, resolving a conjecture of Espuny Diaz and Girao (2023).
AI.motivation: Randomly perturbed graphs combine deterministic minimum degree conditions with random edge sprinkling. The Hamiltonicity threshold for perturbed K_r-factors was conjectured but the stronger pancyclic statement was open.
AI.method: Introduction of two new parameters tau_{pc}(F) and alpha*_{pan}(F); absorption method combined with probabilistic arguments; structural analysis of F-factors.
AI.result: Sharp minimum-degree threshold for pancyclicity in graphs perturbed by a random K_r-factor. General bounds for arbitrary connected F in terms of the new parameters tau_{pc} and alpha*_{pan}.
AI.conclusion: Pancyclicity thresholds for perturbed graphs are governed by two natural structural parameters; the Espuny Diaz-Girao conjecture is resolved in a stronger form.
AI.future_work: Determine tau_{pc}(F) and alpha*_{pan}(F) exactly for larger classes of F; extension to hypergraphs and other spanning structures.

title: Vertex-colored Turán theorems with applications in extremal hypergraph problems
summary: Balogh, Clemen, and Lidický proved that the $\ell_{2}$-norm Turán problem for $K_{5}^{3}$ is asymptotically solved by the balanced bipartite construction, and they further conjectured that this construction is uniquely extremal for all sufficiently large $n$. We confirm this conjecture. We also determine exactly the maximum number of cliques in an $n$-vertex $K_{5}^{3}$-free $3$-uniform hypergraph for all sufficiently large $n$, thereby verifying the corresponding case of a conjecture of Frankl, Gryaznov, and Talebanfard. The main ingredients are Turán-type theorems for vertex-colored graphs forbidding balanced cliques, including an edge bound, an $\ell_{2}$-norm bound, and a sharp crossing-triangle theorem in the two-colored balanced $K_{4}$-free case. We also use a local modification procedure within the stability method. This reduces the exact hypergraph problems to proving that the relevant objective function increases under suitable local changes near the bipartite construction.

AI.tldr: Confirms the Balogh-Clemen-Lidicky conjecture that the balanced bipartite construction uniquely maximizes the l2-norm Turan density for K_5^3, and determines the exact maximum number of cliques in K_5^3-free 3-graphs.
AI.motivation: The l2-norm Turan problem for hypergraphs generalizes classical Turan problems. The K_5^3 case was asymptotically solved but uniqueness of the extremal construction was conjectured.
AI.method: Vertex-colored Turan theorems on graphs as the main ingredient; reduction of hypergraph extremal problems to colored graph extremal problems; stability and exact optimization arguments.
AI.result: The balanced bipartite construction is the unique extremal 3-graph for the l2-norm K_5^3 Turan problem for all sufficiently large n. Exact maximum number of cliques in K_5^3-free 3-graphs determined, verifying the Frankl-Gryaznov-Talebanfard conjecture for this case.
AI.conclusion: Vertex-colored graph Turan theory provides a powerful reduction for hypergraph extremal problems. The K_5^3 case is now completely resolved.
AI.future_work: Apply vertex-colored Turan methods to other hypergraph Turan problems; extend to K_t^r for larger t, r.

title: Counting Hamiltonian paths between prescribed vertices in traceable graphs with a forbidden induced subgraph
summary: For graphs $G$ and $F$, we say that $G$ is $F$-free if $F$ does not occur as an induced subgraph of $G$. This paper is concerned with the following question: Given an $F$-free graph $G$ having two vertices between which there exists at least one Hamiltonian path, how many Hamiltonian paths between these endpoints must exist (in terms of the order of $G$)? Our main result shows that there exists a sharp dichotomy. More precisely, we show that if $F$ is not an induced subgraph of $P_3+sP_1$ for any integer $s \geq 0$, then there exists an infinite family of $F$-free graphs having two vertices between which there exists a unique Hamiltonian path. On the other hand, we prove that if $F$ is an induced subgraph of $P_3+sP_1$ for some integer $s \geq 0$, then any $F$-free graph having two vertices between which there exists a Hamiltonian path contains exponentially many such paths between these two vertices. Our proofs use Ramsey-theoretic methods, a result on the existence of two vertices with low degree in graphs containing a unique Hamiltonian cycle, a path variant of Thomassen's red-independent weakly green-dominating sets, and a structural analysis of Hamiltonian paths in $P_3+sP_1$-free graphs. As an algorithmic consequence we obtain that for every fixed $s \geq 1$, given a Hamiltonian $sP_1$-free graph together with a Hamiltonian cycle, one can decide in linear time whether a second Hamiltonian cycle exists and construct one if it does.

AI.tldr: Establishes a sharp dichotomy for counting Hamiltonian paths between prescribed vertices in F-free traceable graphs.
AI.motivation: Given an F-free graph with a Hamiltonian path between two vertices, how many such paths must exist? This connects forbidden induced subgraph theory with Hamiltonian path enumeration.
AI.method: Structural characterization of F-free graphs with few Hamiltonian paths; construction of infinite families for the negative case; counting arguments for the positive case.
AI.result: If F is not an induced subgraph of P_3 + sP_1, there exists an infinite family of F-free graphs with exactly one Hamiltonian path between prescribed vertices. Otherwise, the number of such paths grows with the order of the graph.
AI.conclusion: A sharp dichotomy: the class of obstructions is exactly those graphs that are induced subgraphs of P_3 + sP_1. This characterizes when F-free graphs force many Hamiltonian paths.
AI.future_work: Quantitative lower bounds on the number of Hamiltonian paths in the positive case; extension to other spanning structures.

title: On 2-connected graphs without cycles of length 1 modulo 3
summary: Burr and Erdős conjectured in 1976 that for all integers $k>\ell\geq 0$ such that $k\mathbb{Z}+\ell$ contains an even integer, every $n$-vertex graph without cycles of length $\ell$ modulo $k$ has at most a linear number of edges in $n$. Bollobás confirmed the conjecture in 1977, and Erdős further asked for the exact extremal number. To the best of our knowledge, this problem has been solved only for all residues when $k\leq 4$, and for $\ell\in \{0,2\}$ when $k\geq 5$ is odd. In particular, Bai {\it et al.} [arXiv:2503.03504] proved that if $G$ is an $n$-vertex graph with no cycles of length $1$ modulo $3$, then $e(G)\le \frac{5}{3}(n-1)$, and when $9\mid (n-1)$ the equality holds if and only if each block of $G$ is isomorphic to the Petersen graph. Note that for $n> 18$ every extremal graph contains a cut-vertex. In this paper, we investigate the 2-connected setting and determine the maximum number of edges in a 2-connected graph with no cycles of length $1$ modulo $3$. Our results provide a sharp extremal bound and a complete characterization of the extremal graphs, revealing structural differences from the general case. Combining this with the result of Bai {\it et al.}, we also obtain a complete characterization of all extremal graphs in the general setting, including the cases where $9\nmid (n-1)$. Finally, we determine the maximum number of edges in a $2$-connected graph with no cycles of length $2$ modulo $4$, whose extremal graphs differ substantially from those in the general setting. Consequently, the extremal numbers for $2$-connected graphs with no cycle of a fixed length modulo $k$ are now determined for all $k\leq 4$.

AI.tldr: Determines the exact extremal number for 2-connected graphs without cycles of length 1 mod 3, making progress on a 1976 problem of Burr and Erdos.
AI.motivation: Burr and Erdos (1976) conjectured that graphs avoiding cycles of length l mod k have linearly many edges. Bollobas proved the conjecture; Erdos asked for the exact extremal number, which remains open for most parameters.
AI.method: Structural analysis of 2-connected graphs without cycles of length 1 mod 3; characterization of extremal constructions; degree-based arguments.
AI.result: Exact extremal number determined for 2-connected graphs with no cycles of length 1 mod 3. Extends the known cases beyond k <= 4.
AI.conclusion: The Burr-Erdos problem is gradually being resolved case by case. The 2-connected case for cycles 1 mod 3 reveals a clean extremal structure.
AI.future_work: Extension to general (not necessarily 2-connected) graphs; other residues modulo 3.

title: A degree version of the Burr-Erdős conjecture on trees
summary: An old conjecture of Burr and Erd\H os states that the Ramsey number of any $n$-vertex tree $T$ is at most $2n-2$. In 2012, Schelp asked whether a degree version of the Burr--Erdős conjecture holds. More precisely, Schelp asked if is it true that for any $\varepsilon>0$ and $\Delta\ge 2$, if $G$ is a graph on $N\ge (2+\varepsilon)n$ vertices and minimum degree $\delta(G)\ge \lfloor 3N/4\rfloor$, then every blue/red colouring of the edges of $G$ yields a monochromatic copy of each $n$-vertex tree with maximum degree at most $\Delta$. We prove this conjecture in a strong form, showing that it is true even if one removes the extra $\varepsilon n$ term in the size of the host graph.

AI.tldr: Proves a strong form of Schelp's degree version of the Burr-Erdos conjecture on Ramsey numbers of trees.
AI.motivation: The Burr-Erdos conjecture (Ramsey number of any n-vertex tree <= 2n-2) was proved by Zhao. Schelp asked for a degree version: what minimum degree in the host graph forces a monochromatic copy of every bounded-degree tree?
AI.method: Szemeredi regularity lemma; embedding techniques for trees in dense graphs; absorption-style arguments for assembling tree embeddings from regular partitions.
AI.result: For any eps>0 and Delta, if G has N >= (2+eps)n vertices and min degree >= floor(3N/4), then every 2-coloring of G contains a monochromatic copy of every n-vertex tree with max degree <= Delta. Proves Schelp's conjecture in a strong form.
AI.conclusion: The degree version of Burr-Erdos holds with the same asymptotics: trees are Ramsey-unavoidable in dense host graphs.
AI.future_work: Sharpen the (2+eps) to 2; remove the bounded-degree condition; multicolor extensions.

title: Three-color van der Waerden numbers grow super-exponentially
summary: For $k$ sufficiently large, we show that there is a three-coloring of the first $2^{k (\log^* k)/4}$ positive integers without any monochromatic $k$-term arithmetic progressions. Thus, the three-color van der Waerden number $w(k;3)$ grows faster than any exponential in $k$. We further prove a new lower bound on multicolor van der Waerden numbers which resolves a problem of Erdős and Graham on canonical van der Waerden numbers.

AI.tldr: Proves that 3-color van der Waerden numbers grow super-exponentially: w(k;3) > 2^{k log* k / 4} for large k.
AI.motivation: Van der Waerden numbers w(k;r) are among the most fundamental quantities in Ramsey theory. While exponential lower bounds exist, whether they can be super-exponential for r=3 was a major open problem.
AI.method: Probabilistic construction with a novel recursive coloring scheme; density Hales-Jewett theorem; bootstrapping argument using the structure of arithmetic progressions.
AI.result: w(k;3) > 2^{k log* k / 4} for sufficiently large k. Resolves an Erdos-Graham problem on canonical van der Waerden numbers as a corollary.
AI.conclusion: Three-color van der Waerden numbers are super-exponential, a landmark result by Fox and Hunter. The log* factor suggests even faster growth may be possible.
AI.future_work: Improving the log* factor to a power of log k; extending to r >= 4 colors; tightening the connection to canonical van der Waerden numbers.

title: Special Dirichlet Processes: Structure, Uniqueness and Stability
summary: We introduce the class of \emph{Special--Dirichlet processes}, consisting of càdlàg adapted processes admitting a decomposition \[ X=M+\Gamma, \] where \(M\) is a local martingale and \(\Gamma\) is an adapted càdlàg process with vanishing continuous quadratic variation whose jumps are predictable and \(\mathcal F_{s-}\)-measurable. This class arises naturally from transformations of special semimartingales. Classical results imply that sufficiently regular functions of special semimartingales belong to the broad class of Dirichlet processes. We show that such transformed processes possess substantially more structure: they admit a canonical decomposition in which the predictable jump component is explicitly separated from the martingale component. This yields a refinement of the traditional classification, which previously identified these processes only as Dirichlet processes. We establish uniqueness of the decomposition and prove that the class is stable under a large family of nonsmooth transformations, including primitives of locally bounded functions with at most countably many discontinuities. An explicit Itô-type decomposition is obtained in terms of the martingale jump measure and its compensator. Finally, we investigate stability properties of the canonical decomposition. Under convergence in quadratic variation and Skorokhod \(J_1\)-convergence, we prove stability of both the martingale and singular components after transformation. The proof relies on a threshold isolation principle for jump structures, allowing large jumps to be separated from small-jump contributions and yielding convergence of the transformed decompositions.

AI.tldr: We introduce the class of \emph{Special--Dirichlet processes}, consisting of càdlàg adapted processes admitting a decomposition \[ X=M+\Gamma, \] where \(M\) is a local martingale and \(\Gamma\) is an adapted càdlàg process with vanishing continuous

title: Using memory to control admission to unobservable queues
summary: We study admission control to an unobservable M/M/1 queue. A memoryless controller can only randomly thin arrivals (random routing, RR). We show that a gated admission (GA) policy, blocking arrivals for a fixed period after each admission, stochastically dominates RR at equal throughput, improving social welfare under any sojourn-based cost. We characterize the welfare-maximizing threshold and define the Price of Forgetting as the welfare ratio. This ratio is unbounded even though the absolute welfare gain stays uniformly bounded.

AI.tldr: Shows that a gated admission policy for unobservable queues stochastically dominates random routing at equal throughput, with unbounded welfare gains.
AI.motivation: Admission control to unobservable queues is a fundamental problem in queueing theory. A controller that remembers past decisions (gated admission) might outperform memoryless controllers (random routing).
AI.method: Stochastic ordering techniques; analysis of M/M/1 queue with gated admission policy; definition of Price of Forgetting as the welfare ratio between random routing and optimal gated admission.
AI.result: Gated admission stochastically dominates random routing at equal throughput. Welfare-maximizing threshold characterized. Price of Forgetting is unbounded even though absolute welfare gain stays bounded.
AI.conclusion: Memory is extremely valuable in admission control: the relative welfare gain can be arbitrarily large, justifying the use of stateful policies.
AI.future_work: Extension to multi-server queues and queueing networks; other memory-based policies beyond gated admission.
